scope: Diagnosis and proposed narrow test-fixture portability correction; no final Windows qualification acceptance

findings.classification: Windows-invalid test-side read of an intentionally held lock file
findings.detail: The complete fixture acquires the publication guard, starts the waiting child, writes a forged higher snapshot_sequence, and calls snapshot_checkpoint before releasing the guard. snapshot_checkpoint reads every file, including root-relative publish.lock. The actual panic is that fs::read unwrap at line 170 with raw OS 33; it occurs before the child's refusal and unchanged-state assertions are reached.
findings.minimal_repair: In snapshot_checkpoint only, recognize exactly the root-relative publish.lock entry. Assert its metadata length is zero and record an empty Vec for that map entry; retain the ordinary exact-byte read for every other path. An empty file has precisely those zero bytes, so the entry and byte-preservation invariant remain represented.
preserve: Publication guard lifetime and child ordering
Forged higher sequence and absence of local publication proof
Expected child exit 4 or 5 and empty stdout
Complete before/after checkpoint map equality including publish.lock

findings.classification: Oversized inline test-fixture argument prevents the intended update subprocess from starting on Windows
findings.detail: Both 40*1024-byte filler calls use set_notes, which forwards the entire payload through --notes. The actual .output().expect failure at line 87 is OS 206. The existing set_notes_via_stdin writes the identical input bytes through --notes-file -, closes stdin and requires process success.
findings.minimal_repair: Change only the two 40 KiB call sites at original lines 507 and 589 from set_notes to the existing set_notes_via_stdin helper. Keep payload generation, byte sizes, loop counts and every shard split/merge/coverage/republication assertion unchanged.
preserve: Exactly the same filler contents and three updates per scenario
96 KiB shard split and 64 KiB per-record assumptions
All issue coverage, byte budgets and shard signatures

findings.classification: Caught harness setup failure; intended split workload remains unqualified
findings.detail: Both recorded RED classifications contain the same OS 206 process-launch failure. Their wrappers completed successfully because the OOB probe catches scenario panics, but these entries do not exercise the intended oversized update and cannot serve as final product characterization. The same shared call-site correction repairs their transport.
